title.narrative: Life-saving treatment and preventive nutrition services provided to children and pregnant and lactating women in drought-affected hotspot areas (Zeylac distirct, Awdal) in northern region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Sept 2025 Somalia FSNAU report, indicates that poor rainfall, flooding and persistent conflicts are driving almost 3.4 million people into high levels of acute food insecurity (IPC P3 or above) across Somalia. Between July and Sept 2025, 624,000 people (3% of the population) have been experiencing Emergency levels of acute food insecurity (IPC P4), while more than 2.8 million people (15% of the population) experiencing IPC P3 (Crisis). ltbrgtltbrgtFrom Oct -Dec 2025 about 23% of the population i.e., 4.4M (921,000 in Emergency P4 3,430,000 in P3) will be facing high levels of acute food insecurity and need urgent action. The June 2025-July 2026 projection estimates 1.85M cases of children aged 6-59 months are expected to suffer acute malnutrition (GAM) (421,000 SAM 1,428,000 MAM) unless if timely and adequately assisted representing 12% increase in GAM and 5% in SAM compared the same season last year.lt/pgtltpgtAwdal Region registers 145,370 IPC3+ out of 655,893 people between Oct-Dec 2025, an increase from 96,440 in July-Sept 2025. Aug 25-July 26 projects 10,480 CU5 in SAM and 42,650 in MAM totaling 53,130 GAM burden out of 131,179 CU5 (FSNAU Sep, 2023). ltbrgtMarket reliance in Awdal (and Zeylac) increases as local production remains limited. Staple food prices are expected to trend above seasonal norms between Oct Dec 2025, driven by low rainfall, reduced labour income, limited stocks high import/transport costs (IPC Oct-Dec 2025). Energy/fuel and firewood costs remain a significant burden for households in Awdal and Zeylac which further strains purchasing power. Poor rainfall and drought conditions led to failed crop production and poor livestock production and reproduction exacerbating the situation. The population is in need of health, nutrition services including prevention treatment, food nutrition security, WASH protection.ltbrgtTo prevent deterioration of human suffering and saving lives, the project will respond to the situation with an objective of increasing safe access to integrated life-saving treatment and preventive nutrition services to the drought affected vulnerable communities in host and displaced areas in Zeylac district, Awdal region by providing nutrition interventions in 13 target villages i.e. (1 static SC at Zeylac Hospital, 5 static OTP in Tokhoshi, Casha Ado, Ceelgaal, Saylac and Habaas Health Center), 1 Mobile at (Zeila IDP, Lantamorohda Daraya Dheere, xuseen, riiga Indhabiraale, Shiekh aware, Geed haad villages) targeting 46,619 individuals (22,673W, 9,973G,4,693M,9280B). The project will screen 11,356(5800W, 2856G and 2700B) children aged below five and PLWs for malnutrition. About795 (415F, 380M) children aged 6-59 months with SAM without medical complication will be admitted to OTP for treatment. The 3,727 (1856 PLW, 895B, 976G) identified with MAM will be referred to TSFP sites implemented by WV. About 5127(2494W, 1096G, 516M and 1021B) PWDs will be given priority. A training of 14 (7M,7M) health workers on IMAM, 26 (13M,13F) on iCCM+ will be done. Will integrate health, protection, WASH, food cash through other partners.ltbrgtOn prevention, will conduct a group individual IYCF sessions through establishing Mother-to-Mother support Groups (M2MSGs) with 100 PLWs as members. Will reach 7,175 people (4792F, 2383M) with IYCF promotion. train 600 caregivers of CU5 on Family MUAC screen refer children to OTPs. Will promote Kobciye Shurbad approach with locally produced foods. Will support supplementation of MNP, MMS, Vit A deworming activities. Will mainstream protection by integrating awareness in ongoing nutrition, training project staffs on SGBV, PSEA for prevention, detection and reporting of protection issues. Will ensure equal access to every vulnerable group implement vulnerability-based targeting for inclusion of marginalized vulnerable groups. All staff will receive AAP orientation and safeguarding. WV has active UNICEF PD and WFP FLA from which will obtain all supplies required for OTPs TSFP.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
